summary: Weekly POC sync for Redwood Private VPC pilot. Reviewed network routing fixes, recent performance runs, and a planned runtime upgrade. SE recommended batching and KV cache tuning; customer to validate KMS access and route table changes. Action items and next steps assigned.
topics: performance results and tuning (batching, KV cache)
transcript:
00:00 Samir Patel: hey everyone, thanks for hopping on. quick roll call?
00:06 Marta Ruiz: Marta here, lead ML eng at Helios.
00:08 Daniel Kim: Daniel, infra.
00:10 Priya Sethi: Priya, security.
00:12 Priya Nair: Priya from Redwood, SE. Samir on the AE side.
00:18 Samir: awesome, agenda — network status, 24-hour bench results, runtime upgrade window, action items. try to keep it to about 45.
00:28 Marta: sounds good, we had one flapping route overnight after the NAT scale change, but it's stable this morning.
00:35 Daniel: yeah we increased the NAT gateway, we still saw some dropped connections when we ran higher qps with the raft test, I think it's route propagation timing more than n at gateway.
00:48 Priya Nair: thanks, so quick note — the issue looked like two things: the VPC peering route table had a missing 10.10.0.0/16 entry for the private nodes, and also the security group stateful rules weren't aligning with the ephemeral ports the runtime opens. we submitted a fix to the infra repo and applied a small rule to allow 31000-32000 ephemeral range. that removed the majority of connection resets in our tests.
01:15 Marta: ok that matches what we saw. after the fix latency tail dropped a bit. do you have the numbers?
01:21 Priya Nair: yes, bench-summary.xlsx — I'll paste link after this call. from yesterday's 10k sample: p50 85ms, p95 230ms, p99 ~460ms for the hosted model path on the pilot infra. after routing fixes p95 dropped to 190 and p99 to ~400. still seeing some outliers at higher token counts.
01:45 Samir: worth calling out the difference between running with cold-starts vs primed KV cache — most of the outliers are cold start token-heavy requests.
01:55 Marta: we did more long-seq tests (2k tokens) and saw p99 jump to 1.1s — that's high for us. are there recommended config changes?
02:05 Priya Nair: definitely. SE recommendations: enable prefix-KV caching for repeated session patterns, reduce batch timeout from 50ms to 30ms for tail-sensitive routes, and consider a quantization profile for your model variant — we have a q4 profile that trades a few points of quality for 20-30% token perf.
02:28 Daniel: are there risks with the q4 profile in terms of correctness for our legal-doc summarization flows?
02:33 Priya Nair: good question, q4 can introduce small semantic drift on very specific tokens — we can run side-by-side A/B on a validation set. recommend start with small sample and check rouge/bertscore thresholds.
02:47 Marta: please do that, send the eval harness.
02:50 Samir: action — Priya will run KV cache tweak + batch change and share CSV, Priya can you also run a 10k-query with the new batching settings?
02:58 Priya Nair: yup, I'll schedule it tonight, should have results by Monday.
03:03 Samir: great. next — runtime upgrade planning. last week we tested the 1.8 runtime build with improved attention kernels. plan is to roll to pilot cluster next Wed night. any blockers?
03:16 Daniel: main blocker is the immutable AMI build pipeline — need to confirm the bootstrap script pulls the right kernel modules for our instance type. also need to ensure we don't break KMS access during rolling restarts.
03:28 Priya Sethi: about KMS — we validated the key policy but there was confusion about which IAM role is allowed to decrypt. currently the role used by the runtime is redwood-pilot-role-prod, but our security policy wants it scoped to the Helios-managed role.
03:42 Samir: ok that matches the security note. we can update the runbook and do a canary with a single node. Priya (SE) can help with the canary steps.
03:50 Priya Nair: yep, can help. we'll do a canary in the pilot-az1 and watch metrics for 15 minutes before rolling. also enable tracing hooks so we can correlate errors.
04:00 Marta: how about audit logs? we need TLS + mTLS for control-plane and audit log forwarding to our SIEM.
04:08 Priya Nair: Redwood Private supports syslog/exporter endpoints; we provide an agent that can forward audit logs to your SIEM over TLS. mTLS is supported for control-plane. I'll send the security integration doc.
04:18 Priya Sethi: please include sample policies for SSO/SAML and RBAC mapping to our internal groups.
04:23 Samir: noted. we'll attach the security pack and SOC2 artifact set.
04:27 Marta: back to perf — any immediate tuning that gives big wins?
04:30 Priya Nair: yes, KV cache + smaller batch timeout, and if you can tolerate q4 for the non-regulatory paths we saw 25% token cost reduction. also enable shard-aware routing so larger requests are sent to nodes with prewarmed KV.
04:44 Daniel: shard-aware routing — is that auto or config?
04:47 Priya Nair: config at the load balancer layer, we have a sample policy in the routing repo. I'll link it.
04:53 Samir: great. any blocker on our side for the rolling upgrade window next Wed?
04:57 Daniel: just need the runbook and the final AMI. if we get those by Monday we can do the canary Wednesday.
05:04 Samir: perfect. we'll send runbook and updated routing diagram.
05:08 Marta: one more item — we hit a 500 error during a bulk inference job when the token buffer exhausted. log says OOM in runtime process.
05:16 Priya Nair: likely memory config — either KV cache size or per-request mem limit. we can add a guard and backpressure, and also tune batch size and split very long requests. for the test job, if you can share the request payload and the logs we'll reproduce in our staging image.
05:29 Marta: ok will upload logs to the shared Drive (link).
05:33 Samir: recap and next steps: 1) Samir send redwood-private-deploy.md, bench-summary.xlsx, routing diagram; 2) Priya SE run KV cache + batching tests and share CSV; 3) Daniel to confirm route table & NAT changes and prepare AMI pipeline details; 4) Marta/Security to validate KMS policy and RBAC mapping.
05:52 Priya Sethi: timeline looks good, we'll prioritize KMS check.
05:55 Samir: any other questions?
05:58 Marta: nope, that's it. thanks team.
06:00 Samir: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with links and schedule a canary for next Wed.
06:05 Meeting ends.
